column1: # naming-exemptions.tsv (harbor#967) — the names in this repo harbor's naming lint does not judge, and why.
# Rows are appended to harbor's standards/naming/exemptions.tsv before the lint runs; same columns, same kinds
# (tool-required, world-name, legacy). A legacy row expires on remove_by and the list only shrinks.
# COLUMNS  id <TAB> rule <TAB> subject <TAB> kind <TAB> remove_by <TAB> reason

column6: reason

this repo's own dogfood of the tree it scaffolds: harnesses read .agents/ by name. It still carries the template names from before harbor#967, because its .agents/hooks/ is write-protected to agent sessions; the rename ships as the operator-applied Deliverables/2026-10-30-merge-and-install/project-init-own-tree-names.patch, after which this row narrows to the harbor-owned names (inject.d/, ship.conf). Not legacy only because a legacy row names one rule
Claude Code reads .claude/ by name; it is the generated mirror of .agents/ (tools/sync_claude_dir.py) and is renamed by the same own-tree patch as yard-0001
the import name of the PyPI package project-init, published on an index and pinned by users
Python import names are snake case; the package is project_init
Mermaid's own extension; the diagram skill and the staleness hooks read .mmd by name

projects-orchestrator reads SCHEMA.md by name as a memory index file (src/projects_orchestrator/memory.py _INDEX_FILES); a lower-case schema.md would be judged a memory note. The rename waits for it to read both
